samples.summary: Divider drag ignores the grab offset, so the divider jumps by up to its (now 25px) width on the first pointermove
samples.evidence: `const ratio = (ev.clientX - rect.left) / track;` maps the pointer x directly onto the *left edge* of pane 1, i.e. onto the divider's left edge. The divider is now 25px wide (`divider.style.width = '25px'`), and a user grabs it anywhere inside that band — typically the centre. On the first `pointermove` the divider snaps so its left edge sits under the pointer, i.e. it jumps left by the grab offset (0–25px, ~12px typical). The change made this strictly worse (7px → 25px) while the new comment claims the mapping is now `ratio * track` "exactly". A correct implementation captures `grabOffset = e.clientX - divider.getBoundingClientRect().left` at pointerdown and subtracts it: `ratio = (ev.clientX - grabOffset - rect.left) / track`.

samples.summary: Shadow-mode log calls `.map` on unvalidated `body.attributes`, turning a malformed body into a 500 instead of the allow-through shadow mode exists to guarantee
samples.evidence: `const target = (body?.attributes ?? []).map(...)` — `YorkieAuthBody` (line 21) is a plain TS interface with no class-validator DTO/ValidationPipe behind it, so `attributes` is whatever JSON arrives. `decide()` tolerates a non-array: `body?.attributes?.length` is truthy for a string and `for (const attr of "abc")` iterates characters, returning a 403 deny. Control then enters the shadow branch, where `"abc".map` is `undefined` → TypeError → 500. Before this change the shadow branch always returned 200/allow. A 500 from the webhook is read by Yorkie as a refusal, which is exactly the lock-out shadow mode is supposed to make impossible during rollout. Reachability is narrow (the endpoint is behind `YorkieSignatureGuard`, and the real Yorkie server always sends an array), hence minor. `Array.isArray(body?.attributes) ? … : []` fixes it.
searchedFor: other uses of body.attributes in decide()/checkAttribute

samples.summary: Neutering `setLocalSelection` silently removes the read-only viewer's caret/selection from peers' screens
samples.evidence: `setLocalSelection` falls into the shared `noop` branch, and `remote-selection.ts:170-172` is the only publisher of local presence selection. On every read-only mount (share-link viewer, revision preview) the viewer's caret/selection is therefore never published, so collaborators lose the "someone is reading here" caret they previously saw for viewer-role visitors — a live behaviour change unrelated to any write on the note's *content* (presence is not in the CRDT text and evaporates on detach). The code comment and docs/design/notes/notes.md call this deliberate, so this is flagged as a regression to weigh rather than an unnoticed bug; if it is intended, nothing in the tests pins it either way.

samples.summary: `readOnly` is derived by a fail-open equality on an untyped `role`, so any role that is not exactly "viewer" gets a writable mount
samples.evidence: `const readOnly = resolved.role === "viewer";` while `ResolvedShareLink.role` is typed `role: string` (packages/frontend/src/api/share-links.ts:8,17). Any present or future role value other than the two known ones (e.g. a "commenter" link, or a typo/rename server-side) yields `readOnly === false`: the formatting group, undo/redo and the share-token uploader all mount, and the writes then get refused by `hasAccess` (`link.role === 'editor'`) once enforcement is on — i.e. a UI that offers edits the server rejects. The backend gate is the inverse (fail-closed: only `editor` may write), so client and server disagree for any third value. Same pattern exists in the sibling layouts, so this is relocated rather than newly introduced, but the new file is where the notes path now decides it.
